title: Heavy chain stitch
subtitle: A bold chain variation where each loop links through the previous two
excerpt: Heavy chain stitch passes the needle under the previous two loops rather than one, creating a denser, raised band that looks more like a plaited cord than a standard chain line.
sourceNotes: Caulfeild and Saward, Dictionary of Needlework (1882). Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopaedia of Needlework (1886).
heroPrompt: Heavy chain stitch forming a bold line on dark fabric, the raised plaited texture visible, cream thread, close-up, natural light.

content.text: Heavy chain stitch does not enter the fabric on every stitch. After the first two links, each new stitch inserts the needle under the previous two loops (not into the fabric) and back into the fabric only at the needle exit point. The chain builds on top of itself, forming a raised plaited band.

items.label: Thread
items.value: Perle cotton no. 5 or 6 strands of stranded cotton

content.text: Work the first two links as plain chain stitch to establish the base.
For the third stitch: slide the needle under both previous links (not through the fabric) and re-insert into the fabric at the point where link 2 exited.
Bring the needle up one stitch-length ahead. Pull through gently so the new loop should lie flat on top of the previous links.
Continue, always passing under the two previous links before each new entry into the fabric.

items.symptom: The band lies flat rather than raised
items.cause: Only passing under one previous link.
items.fix: Check the needle goes under both links before entering the fabric.

items.symptom: The links are loose and floppy
items.fix: Pull each stitch to a firm but not tight tension before starting the next.

content.text: Heavy chain produces a bold raised line suited to stems and outlines in crewelwork. Its plaited texture reads as a cord at normal viewing distance and is an alternative to couching where a raised line is needed.
